topPRs.title: feat(op-conductor-ops): migrate to apko + melange
topPRs.author: falcorocks
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Migrate `op-conductor-ops` from a hand-written `python:3.12-slim-bookworm` Dockerfile to a declarative apko + melange build using upstream Wolfi packages and the factory `apko.yaml` reusable workflow.

The Dockerfile was previously running \`poetry install\` inside the container at **runtime** (every container start), and the launcher script ran a fresh \`poetry install\` again. With apko, every dependency is resolved at build time as a signed Wolfi apk, the wheel is built via PEP 517 (\`python -m build\` → installer), and the main container has no shell, no poetry, and no pip.

## Project changes

- Move flat-file Python modules into a proper \`op_conductor_ops/\` package directory; convert sibling imports (\`from network import …\`) to relative (\`from .network import …\`).
- Wrap the typer entrypoint in a \`main()\` function so it can be registered as a \`[tool.poetry.scripts]\` entry.
- Update \`pyproject.toml\`:
    - Drop \`package-mode = false\`.
    - Add \`version = "0.0.1"\` and \`packages = [{ include = "op_conductor_ops" }]\`.
    - Register the \`op-conductor-ops\` console script at \`op_conductor_ops.cli:main\`.
- Drop the legacy shell launcher that ran \`poetry install\` at container startup. apko-built images install everything at build time.

## Build changes

- Add \`op-conductor-ops/melange.yaml\`. One pipeline step: \`uses: python/build-wheel\`. The PEP 517 frontend reads \`pyproject.toml\` and invokes \`poetry-core\` to produce a wheel. The runtime closure is declared via Wolfi apk names mirroring \`[tool.poetry.dependencies]\`.
- Add \`op-conductor-ops/apko/op-conductor-ops.apko.yaml\`. Pulls \`wolfi-baselayout\`, \`ca-certificates-bundle\`, \`tzdata\`, and the melange-produced \`op-conductor-ops\` apk. Runs as uid 65532 (non-root).
- Update \`.github/images.json\`: add \`op-conductor-ops\` as a \`groups\` entry (\`mode: apko\`, \`services: [op-conductor-ops]\`) and remove it from the Dockerfile-mode \`images\` map.
- Update \`branches.yaml\` + \`tags.yaml\`: replace the legacy \`detect-changes\` / \`parse-tag\` actions with \`factory/actions/plan\` and add a job that calls \`factory/.github/workflows/apko.yaml\` for the \`op-conductor-ops\` group.

## Verified locally

\`\`\`
$ docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 op-conductor-ops:apko-test-amd64 --help
 Usage: op-conductor-ops [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
 CLI for managing OP Conductor sequencers.
   ...
\`\`\`

Image rebuilt cleanly with no manual fiddling. melange's SCA emitted the runtime closure auto-detected from the wheel's METADATA file (no manual \`pip install\` step needed).

## Test plan

- [ ] Branch CI: factory \`plan\` action emits \`op-conductor-ops\` under \`groups_matrix_json\`; \`apko.yaml\` reusable workflow runs and publishes \`us-docker.pkg.dev/oplabs-tools-artifacts/images/op-conductor-ops:<branch>\`
- [ ] Smoke test passes: \`op-conductor-ops --version\` returns successfully
- [ ] Tag push (\`op-conductor-ops/v<semver>\`) builds and publishes the same image at the version tag
- [ ] Existing Dockerfile-mode images (cci-stats, op-acceptor, etc.) keep building unchanged via the \`local\` matrix job

## Pattern

This PR is the first apko migration in this repo. The \`groups\` shape in \`.github/images.json\` plus the dedicated job in \`branches.yaml\` is intended to be reused for subsequent migrations — one group entry + one job per migrated image (or one group with multiple services if they share a melange config).

topPRs.title: ci: standardize image builds on factory plan action
topPRs.author: falcorocks
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Consolidates `branches.yaml` and `tags.yaml` into a single `build-images.yaml` that calls `ethereum-optimism/factory/actions/plan`. The plan action unifies the legacy `detect-changes` (branch / PR pushes) and `parse-tag` (release tag pushes) flows behind a single matrix output, so one job covers every trigger type.

This iteration also collapses the legacy `local` + `fork` build pair into a single `build` job. The factory reusable now exposes a composite `actions/fork-context` action that resolves the effective registry (`canonical` on non-fork, `ttl.sh/<sha>` on fork) and gates GCP auth + provenance attestation internally, so callers no longer need to fork policy at the matrix level. See [factory#37](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/factory/pull/37).

- Pins the factory references (plan action and reusable workflow) to `aced2657632c849ce64a84cc72e3d2940883d374` from `factory#37`.
- Drops `matrix.x || 'default'` passthroughs for inputs that the factory reusable already defaults (`mode`, `target`, `build_args`, `skip_arm64`); only the inputs that `images.json` actually populates (`context`, `dockerfile`, `image_name`) are forwarded explicitly.
- `build` job carries `id-token: write` and `attestations: write` permissions; the reusable will only exercise them on non-fork events thanks to the new `should_authenticate` output of the composite action.
- `images.json` unchanged except for the prior `shared_paths` update.

## Test plan

- [x] CI passes on this PR (non-fork path validates; fork path is symmetric and isolated in the composite action).
- [x] `plan` emits an empty matrix on this PR since only workflow/config files changed and `build` is skipped.
- [ ] After merge, a follow-up PR touching an image source directory builds only the affected images.
- [ ] A release tag (e.g. `proxyd/vX.Y.Z`) builds and tags exactly that image at the parsed version.
